extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, corporate IP managers, and patent examiners (Korea)
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and examination guidelines used by the Korean Intellectual Property Office to determine whether a patent/utility-model application qualifies for expedited examination based on requester type, documentary proof, timing, relevance to business/project/certification, and evidence of practicing the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications on Duties of State or Municipal Governments — eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for expedited examination related to duties of state or municipal governments (including duties of national or public schools and organizations exclusively responsible for technology transfer and commercialization set up in national/public schools).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request is valid only when the requester is the state or municipal government (or the designated organization for tech transfer/ commercialization in national/public schools). If the requester is not such a government/organization, the examiner shall deem the request invalid and order correction within a designated period; if not corrected, the request is dismissed. Applications by national/public schools or their exclusively-responsible organizations shall be treated equivalently. Definitions: national school = established/managed by the state; public school = set up/run by a municipal government. The organization exclusively responsible for tech transfer must be a legal entity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications related to companies certified as venture businesses — eligibility & documentary/timing requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules governing expedited examination requests when an applicant is a company certified as a venture business under the relevant Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key criteria and examiner guidance: (i) Joint filing with at least one certified venture business => accept. (ii) If the certified venture company's name and the applicant's name are identical => accept. (iii) At least one of: filing date, date of request for expedited examination, or date of determination on expedited examination must fall within the certificate's valid period. (iv) Documentary proof: the original confirmation of being a venture business should be used; a copy may be used if recognized identical; an evaluation notice cannot replace the confirmation. (v) Relevance: if there is no correlation between the venture business type and the claimed invention, the request is not accepted; examiner must order correction and may accept if correlation is well-explained. (vi) How to examine correlation: based on requester’s written explanation and evidential documents (business registration certificate, etc.); examiners may compare company overview/main products and claimed invention on the official venture-business confirmation/announcement website; if correlation cannot be found/accepted, order correction. Additional procedural guidance where the company named on the confirmation is not the applicant: if applicant cannot file in company name because company is not a legal entity, the examiner may treat the application as filed by the venture business only when the applicant and the head of the venture business are the same; business registration certificate may be ordered to determine legal entity status (note: registration-number digits 81–87 indicate legal entity).

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-filing changes and special cases for venture-business-based requests
rubrics_metrics.description: When a venture business is added after filing, and special exceptions allowing eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: General rule: to be eligible on the ground of being a venture business, the applicant must have been a venture business when filing the initial application; adding or changing applicants to include a venture business after filing does not make the application eligible. Exception: if the venture business actually practices the claimed invention and has the right to obtain the patent (transfer rights) from the original applicant, the examiner may confirm this and recognize eligibility. The same exception approach applies to innovation businesses, companies with outstanding employee invention compensation systems, and component/material technology developers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications by Inno-Biz (innovation business) — eligibility, timing, proof, and relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidelines for expedited-examination requests filed by companies designated as Inno-Biz under the relevant Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principal rules: (i) Joint application where at least one applicant is an Inno-Biz => recognize request. (ii) If Inno-Biz company name and applicant name are identical => recognize request. If names differ, only those applications that qualify under the venture-business rules (4.6) are eligible. (iii) Timing: the applicant must constitute an Inno-Biz at at least one of the filing date, request date, or determination date. (iv) Documentary proof: original Inno-Biz Confirmation issued by the Small & Medium Business Administration is required; copies acceptable if identical. (v) Relevance: where no relevance exists between business type and claimed invention, the application is not eligible; examiner shall order correction and may accept if relevance is well-explained. (vi) Relevance determination: based on the requester’s written explanation and evidential documents (business registration certificate, etc.); examiners may consult the Inno-Biz certified company information system website to compare business type and invention content; if relevance cannot be confirmed, order correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companies with outstanding employee invention compensation systems — eligibility and proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules for applications filed by companies designated as having outstanding employee invention compensation systems (Invention Promotion Act).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key guidance: (i) Joint filing with at least one applicant so designated => accept. (ii) Where the designated company's title and applicant name are identical => accept; if different, handle under the venture-business rules (4.6). (iii) Timing: the company must hold the designation at least at one of filing date, request date, or determination date. (iv) Documentary proof: original Certificate of Company with Outstanding Employee Invention Compensation System issued by KIPO is required; copy acceptable if identical. (v) Relevance: if the company’s business type is not relevant to the claimed invention, the request is not eligible; examiner will issue a notice to complement the request; if relevancy is explained, accept. (vi) Relevance determination: based on evidential documents attached to the written explanation (business registration certificate, etc.); if relevance cannot be identified, examiner issues a correction order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications related to national new technology development support projects — subject & determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for expedited examination for applications relating to outcomes of specified national technology development support projects or contracts between government institutions and project lead/participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects enumerated include various statutory project types (industrial technological innovation projects, technological innovation projects, energy tech development, new & renewable energy, industrial convergence projects, ICT development projects, national R&D projects, sole-proprietor creative business projects, and other national new technology support projects financed by government). Determination: applications must be related to the direct outcome of the support project. If direct relation is hard to determine but there are documents proving the institution in charge or participating institution has confirmed the relation, the application shall be recognized as eligible. If necessary, consult the division in charge of the project to determine eligibility. Whether the project is government-financed is a relevant consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications related to outcomes of national quality authentication projects (NeP/NeT/industrial convergence) — eligibility and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility for expedited examination when the claimed invention is a direct outcome of national quality authentication/certification projects (new product, new technology, industrial convergence product, or certain agricultural/maritime tech certifications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects listed: (i) products authenticated as new products (NeP), (ii) technologies certified as new technology (NeT), (iii) products certified as industrial convergence products, (iv) patents re: tech accredited as new technology in maritime/fisheries field. Examination guidance: NeP authenticates products with significant economic/technological impact and high performance among commercialized products based on first local tech or substitutes; certification issued by Minister through evaluation per KATS standards. NeT authenticates technologies that enhance performance or improve productivity, typically completed tech with prototype testing and commercializable within two years; certification issued by Minister via Korea Industrial Technology Association. Industrial Convergence Product authentication covers products from creative combination across industries/tech and is certified by the relevant central administrative institution. If it is unclear whether the claimed invention is the direct outcome, the examiner may order verification; however, if it is likely related and there are no special grounds to doubt, the examiner may recognize eligibility without further investigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications forming basis of priority claim under treaty & related PCT/self-designation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance for expedited-examination requests for applications that form the basis of a priority claim under international treaties and for related PCT/self-designation situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should check whether a foreign-filed application claims priority under the Paris Convention based on the Korean application. For PCT-based filings filed claiming priority, a request for expedited examination shall be recognized except for PCT self-designation applications; priority claim can be determined using PCT Form PCT/RO/105. Converted applications, divisional applications, or applications with domestic priority filed based on the treaty-priority-forming application are NOT eligible for expedited examination as they are not the application forming the basis of the treaty priority claim (example provided). For PCT self-designation where a PCT application designates the Republic of Korea, the prior-filed Korean application may be deemed withdrawn after 1 year and 3 months; therefore a request for expedited examination on the prior-filed application will not be recognized. If a prior-filed request was filed, the examiner shall order correction indicating the ground for rejection; if self-designation is not withdrawn within the designated period, the examiner shall dismiss the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claimed invention being practiced or to be practiced by applicant — subject and evidentiary standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Criteria and evidential requirements for expedited-examination requests where the claimed invention is being practiced or prepared to be practiced by the applicant (including special statutory categories: parts/materials-specialized companies, government-supported competition awardees, component/material technology development businesses, start-ups, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subjects: includes statutory categories (e.g., parts·materials-specialized companies where the claimed invention relates to that business; inventions awarded in government-hosted open contests/competitions if financially supported by government for commercialization or patent filing). Definitions & standards: 'practicing' is identical to practicing by a person other than the applicant; 'practicing as a business' means running a business — personal/domestic/educational/one-time experimental practice generally do not constitute business practice, unless a one-time non-profit practice is carried out as business for public interest. Determination procedures: requester must explain that the invention is being practiced or prepared to be practiced as a business in the written expedited-examination explanation and submit evidential documents. Examiner recognizes practicing/preparation where the explanation and evidential documents confirm the practice. Types of admissible evidence for practicing (or preparing) include written explanation, photos of prototypes, catalogs, product manuals, samples. For practicing-as-business recognition, admissible evidential documents include examples such as business license, transaction sheets indicating the product matches claimed invention, delivery confirmation, purchase contracts, product supply agreements, plant registration certificates, investment records, loan issuance, agreements related to practicing (subject, period, place, condition), lease-rental agreements, evidential documents on component/material technology development business, and other evidence. Special case for construction-field new-technology accreditation: record document management number and concerned art in request form; field-applicability or test data and relevant KAIA webpage references may suffice to deem practiced. Identicalness requirement: the invention being practiced (or prepared to be practiced) must be identical to the claimed invention; requester must prove identicalness via articles, photographs, or other evidential documents plus written explanation; if identity cannot be confirmed, examiner shall order correction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition of applications filed by companies confirmed as component & material technology development businesses
rubrics_metrics.description: Special recognition rules for companies confirmed as component & material technology development businesses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A request for expedited examination by a company so confirmed is accepted as being practiced or prepared to be practiced as a business without submission of the general evidential documents listed above. Relevancy between parts·materials-specialized business and the claimed invention is determined based on proving documents (business license, etc.) enclosed in the expedited request form and, if necessary, by referring to the Korea Institute for Advancement of Technology network. If relevancy cannot be checked/confirmed, examiner shall propose supplement. Joint-filing rules apply (if one applicant is such a company, accept) but acceptance when company name and applicant name differ follows the venture-company rules (4.6) mutatis mutandis. Timing requirement: at least one of filing date/request date/determination date the company must hold the confirmation. Documentary proof: original confirmation required, copy acceptable if identical.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government-supported competition awardees and start-ups — simplified acceptance rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules granting expedited-examination acceptance without the usual evidential documents for inventions awarded in government/open competitions with government financial support and for certain start-ups receiving governmental funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government contest awardees: A patent application for an invention awarded in an open contest/competition hosted/run by the government/local government shall be accepted as being practiced or to be practiced without submission of proving documents, provided the invention is financially supported by government/local government for commercialization or patent filing. Determination of relevance to an awarded invention is based on the expedited request form and enclosed proving documents (certificate of merit, award selection announcement, financial support document, etc.). If all inventions awarded in a contest are known to receive commercialization/patent-filing benefit and this can be proven otherwise, the proving documents need not be filed. Start-ups: (partial content in chunk) Examiner determines start-up status where the application has government financial support over a threshold (example: over 10 million won) for technology development/commercialization or is filed by early-stage start-ups funded under specified Acts — such support may be grounds for expedited handling (text truncated in chunk).
